Add Two Numbers (digits stored in reverse order)

Grade-school addition with a carry. Keeping carry != 0 in the loop condition handles a final extra digit (99 + 1). O(max(m, n)). If digits are stored most-significant first, push both lists onto stacks (or reverse them) first.
Reorder List (L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln-1 …)
Combines three building blocks interviewers love: find middle, reverse, merge. O(n) time, O(1) space. Remember to cut the list at the middle (slow.next = null) or you create a cycle.
Copy List with Random Pointer (deep copy)

The map from original to clone lets you wire random pointers that point forward or backward. O(n) time and space. The O(1)-space version interleaves clones (A → A' → B → B'), sets A'.random = A.random.next, then splits the two lists. The same "old → new map" idea solves Clone Graph.
Reverse Nodes in k-Group
Check that k nodes exist, reverse them with prev starting at the node after the group (so the reversed tail already links forward), then reattach. O(n) time, O(1) space.
Sort List in O(n log n) (merge sort on a linked list)

Merge sort suits linked lists: no random access is needed and merging needs no extra array. O(n log n) time, O(log n) recursion stack (bottom-up merge sort makes it O(1)). Quick sort is a poor fit because partitioning needs random access.
Remove Duplicates from a Sorted List (keep one / remove all)
Version I just skips equal neighbours. Version II needs a dummy head because the first node itself may be removed. Both are O(n) time, O(1) space.
